newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas holds on cold forecasts in East.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas holds on cold forecasts in East.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices held mostly steady Thursday, supported by cold weather weekend forecasts in the East but tempered by the return of nuclear power and ample storage supplies in the East, industry sources said.
Gulf Coast prices remained in the high-$2.60s to low-$2.70s as the Northeast awaited temperatures as much as 15 degrees below-normal this weekend.
The impending cold failed to panic any buyers since storage in the East was near full and a number of nuclear plants along the East Coast returned to service.
American Gas Association (AGA) reported late Wednesday that working gas inventories in the East were up 22 billion cubic feet (bcf) to 96 percent of capacity.
In the Midcontinent, where producing region stocks were still at only 74 percent full, prices were steady to slightly higher in the high-$2.50s to low-$2.60s.
Forecasters are calling for temperatures as much as 12 degrees Fahrenheit below-normal this weekend in most of the Midwest.
The expected cold weather also kept Chicago city-gate prices steady in the $2.85-2.90 area.
In west Texas, prices were also stable in the mid-$2.50s, stalled by cooler weather in the East but more moderate weather on the West Coast.
AGA's data indicated another negative in western storage inventories, falling five bcf to 69 percent of capacity.
At the southern California border, gas traded again in the low-to-mid $2.70s as supplies remained tight in the northwestern U.S.
On the opposite coast, New York city-gate prices held in the mid-$2.90s, while Appalachian prices hovered in the high-$2.80s to mid-$2.90s.
Separately, Niagara Mohawk Power Corp reported earlier Thursday its 610 megawatt Nine Mile Point nuclear power unit 2 in Scriba, N.Y., has reached full power.
